thread:
alex: FYI getting multiple customer reports of 5xx/timeouts hitting the hosted inference API (generation endpoint). spikes started ~09:12 PST 

maya: seeing the same in dashboards — 502/504s from the api-gateway and increased latency to prefix-cache calls :thinking_face: 

monitoring-bot: [ALERT] prefix-cache.redis.latency > 200ms for 95th percentile (09:12:18)

deploy-bot: rolling deploy to inference-rs not in progress right now (no recent deploys logged)

devon: can someone grab recent nginx/gateway logs and prefix-cache logs? suspecting Redis/memcached dependency causing upstream 5xxs

alex: pasted an example of the gateway error from an affected request:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. connection reset by peer
API-Request-ID: r-9b3f2
```

maya: prefix-cache (our KV layer) reports timeouts on GETs for many prefixes. errors look like `read timeout` and `EOF` in the client.

devon: grabbing logs from prefix-proxy:
```
09:12:22 WARN prefix-proxy: redis backend timeout (cmd=GET, key=prefix:abc123) duration=350ms
09:12:23 ERROR prefix-proxy: fallback to origin due to redis timeout key=prefix:abc123
```

robin-oncall: marking incident, paging infra-sre. I'm going to try a quick mitigation: increase redis connection pool and enable short-circuit fallback in prefix-proxy for heavy keys to reduce queueing.

customer-success-anna: we have two customers affected (AcmeCorp, BrightHealth) — they've opened tickets complaining about 5xxs and generation failures. I'm sending a holding message.

alex: repro steps I used: 1) call POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-v1 and long prompt 2) observe 502 after KV GET timeout 3) curl to prefix cache directly shows elevated latency

devon: noted a burst of long-running Lua scripts on Redis at 09:11:50 — looks like a maintenance job/tracer maybe? running `EVALSHA` and slowlog shows commands ~300ms+

robin-oncall: I'm going to failover reads to replica and restart the prefix-proxy pool. doing failover now (manual).

monitoring-bot: [INFO] redis-primary marked read-only; promoting replica for reads at 09:13:12

maya: after triggering failover, p95 for prefix-cache latency dropped from 210ms -> 65ms within ~30s. gateway 5xxs are decreasing. :thumbsup:

devon: opened a postmortem ticket and added short-term mitigation: (1) avoid long Lua scripts in cron jobs, (2) add rate-limiter on heavy prefix keys, (3) tune client timeouts and circuit breaker thresholds.

customer-success-anna: sent update to affected customers: "We're seeing reduced errors after failing over cache reads. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause and timeline."

alex: final note: root cause looks like intermittent Redis slow commands + connection saturation from a background job. follow-ups: full slowlog analysis, audit background jobs, add automated traffic shaping for prefix-cache, consider per-tenant connection pools.

robin-oncall: closing this Slack thread, will keep postmortem in incidents. If anyone sees new regressions ping me. :white_check_mark:
